evals.prompt: Can you turn my pipeline notes into a README with a diagram of the steps?
evals.expected_output: Writes a markdown README with an embedded Mermaid flowchart (accTitle/accDescr, classDef only, no %%{init} or inline style, snake_case node IDs). Follows the markdown style guide, with one H1 and emoji on H2 headings only.

evals.prompt: I'm drafting analysis_report.md for our RNA-seq differential expression results (12 samples, DESeq2). I want it to be git-diffable, with a methods section, a footnoted reference list, and a figure showing how the reads go from FASTQ to the count matrix. I tried `radar` for comparing three aligners across five metrics and GitHub says there's a parse error. Please fix it.
evals.expected_output: Starts from the research paper template and replaces the broken `radar` with valid `radar-beta` syntax (`axis` and `curve` definitions), with a descriptive italic paragraph above it instead of accTitle/accDescr. Adds a Mermaid flowchart for the FASTQ-to-counts pipeline and uses [^N] footnotes with full URLs.

evals.prompt: We have a grant proposal with milestones spread over 18 months and overlapping work packages, and I'd like reviewers to see the schedule at a glance in the doc itself, without pasting in an image.
evals.expected_output: Picks a Mermaid Gantt chart, preferring it over a flowchart or an image, and embeds it inline in the markdown document with accTitle/accDescr and classDef-based styling. It follows the Gantt reference and keeps the text source as canonical.

evals.prompt: Run a systematic literature review on CRISPR base editing off-target effects, searching PubMed and bioRxiv, screening the papers, and give me a PRISMA-style summary with verified citations.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a systematic review task and hands it to the literature-review skill. It does not use the Mermaid/markdown authoring skill as the primary workflow.

evals.prompt: Make a scatter plot of my 5,000 single-cell UMAP coordinates colored by cluster, publication quality.
evals.expected_output: Uses Python plotting (matplotlib/seaborn or similar) for real-data scatter plots, not Mermaid.
